    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Air Canada Posted A Record $6.984 Billion Quarter While Its Basic Business Class Strips Out Flexibility & eUpgrades

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1605 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that air Canada closed the third quarter of 2026 with record operating revenue of $6.984 billion, up 21% from the same period last year.
    • In a recent development, A more useful question for travelers is what a Basic business ticket actually removes, and whether Air Canada’s version requires fewer sacrifices than those of Delta Air Lines and JetBlue, both of which have built similar premium tiers.
    • In a recent development, passenger revenue reached roughly $6.3 billion, driven by yield up 11%, passenger load factor rising 2.6 percentage points to 89.1%, and cargo revenue growing 33%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that air Canada closed the third quarter of 2026 with record operating revenue of $6.984 billion, up 21% from the same period last year. The figure invites an easy narrative that the airline’s fresh Basic fares in business class and premium economy, introduced in late July, fueled the gain, but the evidence published so far does not support that conclusion.

    In a recent development, A more useful question for travelers is what a Basic business ticket actually removes, and whether Air Canada’s version requires fewer sacrifices than those of Delta Air Lines and JetBlue, both of which have built similar premium tiers. Answering it requires looking first at what the quarterly results do and do not say, then at the fare rules themselves, and finally at how competing airlines have drawn the line between the seat and everything around it.

    In a recent development, passenger revenue reached roughly $6.3 billion, driven by yield up 11%, passenger load factor rising 2.6 percentage points to 89.1%, and cargo revenue growing 33%. Unit revenue climbed 14% on both a total and a passenger basis, a gain that arrived on top of capacity growth of 5.7%. Those figures describe an airline filling more seats at higher prices, a pattern consistent with a record quarter. All figures were reported by the airline.

    Industry observers note that profitability told a different story, as fuel expense rose by $906 million while the price per liter climbed from 88.3 cents to 148.3 cents, and operating income slipped to $261 million from $284 million, compressing the operating margin to 3.7% from 4.9%. Adjusted EBITDA of $936 million landed slightly below last year’s $961 million, with the margin falling to 13.4% from 16.6%, while net income attributable to shareholders dropped to $139 million from $264 million and free cash flow turned negative by $440 million.

    Updated Full-Year 2026 Guidance.

    Prior Full-Year 2026 Guidance (Provided on August 11, 2026).

    Approx. 2.75% increase from 2025.

    2.25% to 3.25% increase from 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that management responded by lowering its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $2.4 billion to $2.7 billion, down from $2.9 billion to $3.2 billion, and attributed the change chiefly to higher expected fuel prices. The chief financial officer credited decisive pricing, capacity, and cost actions with softening the fuel impact, a phrase that describes recovering cost pressure rather than capturing premium leisure demand. Balance sheet actions continued alongside the operating results, as Air Canada used Aeroplan transaction proceeds to repay $1.7 billion of debt and completed an $800 million issuer bid that reduced shares outstanding by about 10%.

    Executives reported that premium cabin revenue rose 19% and corporate revenue 22%, with North American markets posting the strongest unit revenue gains because shorter booking windows let the airline pass higher fuel costs into fares more quickly. Premium travel was already central to the airline’s economics, accounting for about 30% of passenger revenue in its 2025 results despite occupying far fewer seats than economy. The trend also predates the Basic launch, since premium revenue grew 11% in the second quarter, when no premium Basic fares existed.

    Sources indicate that chief Commercial Officer Mark Galardo pointed to a behavioral shift, saying that premium customers, whether traveling for leisure or business, have been flying more in spring and autumn than during the summer peak. He described the quarter as a story of premium rather than budget passengers, and he predicted record September and October revenue. Galardo added that the shift began two or three years ago, has accelerated, and is now appearing slightly in November.

    On the fresh fares, Galardo said in mid-August that it was far too early to judge reception because they had been on sale for barely more than a week, and he described United Airlines' early results with its own premium Basic fares as interesting. Because Air Canada’s Basic fares were on sale for only about the last nine weeks of a 13-week quarter, and because fuel-driven fare increases and shifting travel patterns were operating simultaneously, the sources reviewed provide no basis for crediting unbundling with the revenue gain.

    In a recent development, business Class Basic is sold on flights within Canada, to the United States, and to and from Central and South America, and it is not offered on long-haul itineraries such as Montreal to New Delhi. Tickets are non-refundable and carry no future travel credit, while changes up to two hours before departure cost $200 within Canada or to the US and $700 on international flights, in Canadian dollars. Same-day airport changes and standby are not permitted, advance seat selection carries a fee, and the checked allowance falls from two bags to one on Canada and US routes. Carry-on allowances remain at one personal article and one standard article across Basic, Standard, and Latitude.

    According to recent reports, despite the cuts, the fare remains more than critics might expect, since passengers retain Maple Leaf Lounge access, priority check-in and baggage handling, and the same earning rate of one Aeroplan point and four Status Qualifying Credits per dollar. Premium Economy Basic is stricter because it drops lounge access, keeps the same flexibility limits, and, according to AwardWallet, excludes eUpgrade certificates. The business class table lists no eUpgrade row, which makes sense because no cabin sits above it, so the restriction mainly affects travelers who would otherwise apply certificates to a Premium Economy ticket. The savings are modest; on Toronto to Mexico City, AwardWallet found Basic at $1,022, Standard at $1,093, and Latitude at $1,256, leaving only a $71 gap between Basic and Standard, a spread that AwardWallet interprets as a nudge toward the pricier option.

    Recent findings suggest that delta began selling Basic Business on July 8 for travel starting in September, and the fare preserves the lie-flat seat, Zone 1 boarding, and the standard Delta One meal while removing most of the ground experience. Seats are assigned after check-in, the checked allowance shrinks by one bag, and the ticket earns 2 SkyMiles per dollar instead of 5, although it still counts toward Medallion status. Delta also bars upgrades of every kind, paid ones included, and rules out same-day confirmed changes and standby. Delta First Basic has been flying since July in select domestic and Latin American markets, while Premium Select Basic follows alongside Basic Business in September.

    Lounges mark the sharpest contrast, since Basic Business passengers keep Delta One check-in and the Delta One Lounge only through January 18, 2027, after which the privileges lapse unless obtained through a Sky Club membership or an eligible American Express card. Fees also differ, as AwardWallet reports that Delta raised the change and cancellation charge for Basic Business to $500 from $99 on travel originating in the United States and Canada, with cancellations yielding an eCredit toward a future ticket.

    Measured against those terms, Air Canada’s version asks for less on several frontsbecause it retains lounge access, preserves full Aeroplan earnings, and charges $200 for changes within Canada or to the US, versus Delta’s $500. Its $700 international change fee, roughly US$496, is comparable to Delta’s, and its lack of any refund or credit is harsher than Delta’s eCredit. Air Canada also confines Basic to shorter routes, whereas Delta extends its premium Basic fares to select long-haul international markets.

    Sources indicate that jetBlue Airways sorts travelers first by onboard experience, choosing among Main, EvenMore, BlueFirst, and Mint, and then by up to three fare options named Base, Standard, and Flex that differ in seat selection and refundability. Base fares omit seat selection and return travel credit on cancellation, less any fee, and they are branded for Main, EvenMore, and BlueFirst. President Marty St. George framed the structure as two clicks: the onboard experience first and the fare second, according to the release.

    The release states that Base fares are not available in Mint, so the lie-flat product keeps only its Standard and Flex tiers, and a Mint Base fare does not appear in JetBlue’s own description. BlueFirst, the domestic first-class product that begins rolling out later this year, is listed with a Base option, although JetBlue indicates fuller fare details will follow. United, which introduced unbundled premium fares in April 2026, and Lufthansa already sell comparable products, and Air Canada’s tiers resemble those of its partners.

    The fourth-quarter report in early 2027 will be the first to cover a full quarter with Basic fares on sale, which should give analysts a cleaner view than the partial exposure in the third quarter. The reading will be clouded because Air Canada has stated it is not yet providing 2027 guidance and has trimmed planned first-quarter 2027 capacity by two points; fuel prices remain the key variable in its outlook, and a newly introduced chief executive, Anko van der Werff, is due to arrive by the end of January 2027.

    In a recent development, within that noise, the most informative signal may be how many buyers choose Standard when the gap is as small as $71, a figure airlines rarely disclose that would show whether Basic is expanding the premium audience or repricing existing buyers. Delta’s lounge cutoff on January 19, will supply a parallel test of how travelers react to losing ground perks, and Air Canada, having kept its lounge access, can treat that contrast as either a selling point or a cushion for tightening its terms later. Because the incoming chief executive will inherit both the fare structure and the missing 2027 outlook, his first budget cycle may decide whether Basic remains a modest entry point or grows into the fare most travelers see first in search results.

    Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov.
    • Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen.
    • Industry observers note that the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images).

    Former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

    Industry observers note that the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

    With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

    “As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola said in a statement after the race was called.

    The Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

    Industry observers note that peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

    Sources indicate that she entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

    She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

    But the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The Fresh York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

    Peltola has mentioned she had no connection to the scheme.

    According to recent reports, prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

    Trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

    Industry observers note that the Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

    But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

    "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer said in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot.".

    Recent findings suggest that in other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

    According to recent reports, the race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A upcoming deal with Miami-Dade County will help American Airlines solidify and eventually expand its maintenance operations at Miami International Airport.

    Sources indicate that the county confirmed this week that it will buy a hangar and maintenance space at Miami International from a third-party owner and lease it directly to American for its MRO operations. The acquisition includes Hangar 890, Building 891, 10.2 acres of land, and a 2.2-acre parking lot.

    Industry observers note that according to the Miami Herald, American already leases the property and uses it for maintenance work, but a change in ownership from private jet operator Aero Miami to the county will give American more leeway to develop the space as it sees fit. The new lease with the county will run for 20 years and cost American $67.8 million, the newspaper mentioned.

    The airline intends to keep more than 650 aircraft maintenance workers at the facility. It has also agreed to complete about $13.9 million in building repairs.

    According to recent reports, “Miami is a cornerstone of American’s international network and a consequential part of our long-term growth strategy,” American Senior Vice President of Miami Operations Juan Carlos Liscano said in a news release. “This agreement reinforces our dedication to our Miami team and preserves our ability to continue growing our network to more destinations around the world for our customers.”.

    American is the largest airline at Miami, carrying more than half of all passengers there.

    Tech Report: The 7 Largest US Air Force Bases By Land Area

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The USAF has some of the largest and most famous military bases anywhere in the world.
    • As the largest air force of any military on the planet, the USAF not only has thousands of aircraft but also numerous ballistic missile sites and extensive facilities to support operations and logistics.
    • In a recent development, fairchild AFB is located just southwest of Spokane, Washington.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The USAF has some of the largest and most famous military bases anywhere in the world. But when it comes down to size, the question is which one is ultimately the largest of all the air bases. In this article, we are going to break down the seven biggest pieces of real estate owned by the USAF anywhere in the world.

    As the largest air force of any military on the planet, the USAF not only has thousands of aircraft but also numerous ballistic missile sites and extensive facilities to support operations and logistics. Let's get down to it and go down the list, starting with the smallest entry first.

    In a recent development, fairchild AFB is located just southwest of Spokane, Washington. The base is a critical component of the Air Mobility Command and serves as one of the largest aerial refueling hubs in the USAF. The host unit, the 92nd Air Refueling Wing, operates a large fleet of KC-135 Stratotanker aircraft.

    The base is also home to the Air Force's only Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape School. This facility trains roughly 20,000 students annually on how to survive being shot down and captured under the worst conditions possible.

    Industry observers note that the 36th Rescue Squadron supports both the SERE School and the entire Pacific Northwest region across a four-state area. The Air National Guard's 141st Air Refueling Wing and the Joint Personnel Recovery Agency, as well as an Armed Forces Reserve Center, are all located at Fairchild AFB.

    Recent findings suggest that kirtland AFB is home to the nuclear command and Logistics arm of the Air Force Global Strike Command. The unit is a critical component of the US nuclear triad. The Space Force's Delta 15 is headquartered at Kirtland. The base is one of the largest employment sources in the state of Latest Mexico, with 20,000 personnel, including troops and civilians.

    The base also hosts the Air Force Research Laboratory Directed Energy Directorate and the Space Vehicles Directorate. These units are focused on the development of advanced laser, microwave, and space-based technology.

    The base supports over 100 mission partners and units. These include the Department of Energy's Sandia National Laboratories and Los Alamos National Laboratory, the Defense Nuclear Weapons School, and various Air National Guard and Reserve units.

    It has been revealed that edwards AFB is very deep in the Mojave Desert of Southern California, where it is home to around people doing some of the most advanced flight testing and research performed anywhere in the world. The base hosts the US Air Force Test Pilot School as well as NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in the Air Force Research Laboratory. A number of government agencies and leading aerospace companies like Lockheed Martin, Boeing, and Northrop Grumman maintain permanent facilities on their campus.

    It has been revealed that edwards is the headquarters for the Air Force Test Center. The bed of Rogers Dry Lake provides a 65-square-mile natural runway that offers a virtually perfect emergency landing area as well as a testing surface for many experiments. The base also has the largest anechoic chamber in the world for testing aircraft electronic and radio frequency systems.

    Recent findings suggest that air Force Captain Chuck Yeager was the first human being to break the sound barrier when he flew the Bell X-1 rocket plane over the speed of sound at Edwards AFB in 1947. Since then, Edwards has been at the forefront of jet development, with the X-Plane series of increasingly faster supersonic prototypes being developed at the base.

    The development of stealth technology also had its first steps at Edwards with the Lockheed Martin F-117 Nighthawk in the 1980s. Lockheed’s Skunk Works division also developed the F-22 Raptor and F-35 Lightning II at Edwards. Northrop Grumman tested the B-2 Spirit stealth bomber extensively at Edwards, and its successor, the B-21 Raider, is now flying over its airfield.

    NASA and Lockheed are testing the X-59 QueSST (Quiet Supersonic Technology) at Edwards, which is working toward a low-boom design that will allow for renewed supersonic commercial aircraft development. It took its first flight at the end of October 2025. The base was even home to the NASA space shuttle program until 1991.

    Located in the northwest corner of Florida, dubbed the Panhandle, Eglin AFB is the primary test and evaluation center for all USAF weapons, navigation, and guidance systems. This installation hosts almost 20,000 military, civilian, and contractor personnel from the Air Force, Army, and Navy. The Space Force also has an AN/FPS-85 radar on the campus for space surveillance.

    The Air Force Special Operations Command has a large presence on the base, including the Air Force's only Reserve Special Operations Wing, the 919th. The 33rd Fighter Wing is located on the base, which is a joint training unit for both pilots and maintainers of the Lockheed Martin F-35A Lightning II.

    Recent findings suggest that to facilitate the weapons-centric mission of Eglin AFB, the base manages a vast overwater range extending into the Gulf of Mexico. McKinley Climatic Laboratory tests aircraft and equipment under severe weather conditions, and the Air Force Research Laboratory's Munitions Directorate calls Eglin home as well.

    According to recent reports, hill AFB manages the Utah Test and Training Range, which is a 1,490-square-mile expanse of desert used for testing and tactical training. Hill AFB is home to the first F-35 fighter wing that became operational in the USAF, the 388th Fighter Wing. The 75th Air Base Wing is responsible for running Hill AFB facilities.

    In a recent development, the Ogden Air Logistics Complex at Hill AFB manages the life cycle sustainment of the Lockheed F-22 Raptor, F-35 Lightning II, F-16 Fighting Falcon, C-130 Hercules, and A-10 Thunderbolt II. The command is also responsible for the Minuteman III Intercontinental Ballistic Missile.

    Industry observers note that the 419th Fighter Wing of the US Air Force Reserve is also stationed at Hill AFB. The wing flies the F-16 'Viper,' as the jet is nicknamed, and deploys alongside active-duty units to support combat forces. As many as 20,000 troops and civilians work on the base to support the mission of all the different units stationed at Hill AFB.

    The Barry M. Goldwater Air Force Range is one of the premier military training ranges in the United States. The enormous base is used for realistic combat training, not only for US service branches, but also for allied partner nations' militaries. The vast expanse of the range allows for extensive real-world, live-fire air-to-air and air-to-ground tactical training. Around 15,000 people work at the range of the bases associated with it.

    According to recent reports, in addition to being instrumental as a joint forces, combined arms combat training facility, the base allows for advanced electronic warfare and other tactical scenarios. The range is jointly managed by both Luke AFB and Marine Corps Air Station Yuma. The Army National Guard also uses the range extensively. Almost all Marine Corps Aviation units train at this base before deployment to combat theaters.

    Industry observers note that luke AFB is the primary fighter pilot training facility in the US Air Force. The base also recently transitioned to be the main training center for the F-35A Lightning II aircraft for both US pilots and pilots from any of the 19 other nations that also operate the Joint Strike Fighter, as the F-35 is also known. The base is home to the 56th Fighter Wing, which is the largest fighter wing in the USAF.

    It has been revealed that the main facility of Nellis AFB is situated in the northeastern corner of the Las Vegas Valley, hosting 15,000 troops and civilian staff. The base has long been a hub for advanced combat Aviation training. Every year, the International Air Warfare exercise known as 'Red Flag' is held at Nellis.

    According to recent reports, this airfield is home to the Air Force Warfare Center as well as the 99th Air Base Wing and the aerial demonstration team known as the Thunderbirds. The gargantuan military complex includes the Nevada Test and Training Range, Creech AFB, and the Tonopah Test Range (TTR).

    In addition to hosting foreign Air Forces for joint training exercises, the base has a permanent presence of other services, including the Navy, Army, and Marine Corps. Sandia National Laboratories is also located on the base complex, within the boundaries of the TTR facility. NTTR encompasses approximately 3 million Acres of restricted airspace and land, which is home to the famed, highly classified Area 51 (Groom Lake), as well as the TTR.

    These facilities have been instrumental in the development of iconic Advanced aircraft like the Lockheed U-2 Dragon Lady, SR-71 Blackbird, and F-117 Nighthawk. In addition to the Skunk Works projects, Area 51 hosts captured aircraft from adversaries that are reverse-engineered.

    Sandia National Laboratories is part of the US Department of Energy. Its primary mission is to ensure the maintenance, security, safety, and reliability of the US nuclear weapons stockpile. The laboratory also contributes to the development of border security technology, renewable energy technology, missiles, advanced computing, satellites, and spacecraft.

    According to recent reports, creech is located in Indian Springs, 45 miles north of the main base. It serves as a hub for the testing of remotely piloted aircraft and forthcoming collaborative combat aircraft. The vast expanse of the base exists as a safety buffer as well as a physical barrier that enhances the secrecy of the classified activities by leveraging simple geography.

    Industry observers note that the massive range includes numerous Military Operations Areas and Restricted Areas that are used for a myriad of military training activities as well as research and development. Aircraft, missiles, drones, and other weapon systems are all tested, developed, and stored within the grounds of Nellis AFB.

    SFO’s Airfield Will Flood Amid Thanksgiving Rush With 9-Foot Tides Predicted, Officials Say

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Francisco International Airport (SFO) is facing a significant coastal flooding threat during one of the busiest travel periods of the year, with officials warning that exceptionally high tides could overwhelm vulnerable sections of its airfield.
    • It has been revealed that unusually high king tides, storm surge, warmer ocean temperatures, and an approaching winter storm are raising concerns about the airport's ability to keep its airfield and surrounding infrastructure clear of seawater.
    • According to the Los Angeles Times, both SFO and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK) are facing potential flooding as exceptionally high tides approach Northern California.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Francisco International Airport (SFO) is facing a significant coastal flooding threat during one of the busiest travel periods of the year, with officials warning that exceptionally high tides could overwhelm vulnerable sections of its airfield. The National Weather Service (NWS) is forecasting water levels approaching nearly 10 feet or potentially higher around San Francisco Bay between Tuesday and Thursday, coinciding with the Thanksgiving travel rush.

    It has been revealed that unusually high king tides, storm surge, warmer ocean temperatures, and an approaching winter storm are raising concerns about the airport's ability to keep its airfield and surrounding infrastructure clear of seawater. Although SFO is preparing for potential flooding, the situation could create additional complications for passengers, airlines, and airport operations during the holiday period.

    According to the Los Angeles Times, both SFO and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK) are facing potential flooding as exceptionally high tides approach Northern California. NWS meteorologists warned of extreme coastal flooding along the San Francisco Bay shoreline, with water levels potentially exceeding nine feet depending on the storm surge. The forecast is concerning because SFO's seawalls are not uniformly high, leaving certain sections more vulnerable to overtopping.

    According to Deep Arrival, NWS also warned that water levels along SFO's shoreline could reach approximately 9.9 feet (three meters) during the most concerning periods. The airport's seawall stretches for more than seven miles, but some vulnerable sections are reportedly only 8 feet high. The southeastern corner near Runway 28 Left is particularly exposed, while the northern ends of both runways also feature lower sections. It remains unclear whether the runways or taxiways themselves will experience flooding.

    The airport is already preparing for the possibility of seawater entering its airfield. SFO spokesperson Doug Yakel noted the airport was prepared to respond and maintain safe operations, according to Deep Arrival. Crews are clearing drainage areas, inspecting pump stations, and positioning sandbags and emergency flood barriers.

    The flooding threat is being driven by several overlapping weather and astronomical factors. The NWS explains that unusually high king tides, thermal expansion from warmer ocean temperatures, and storm surge are combining to push bay water levels toward historic territory. According to its forecast discussion on Sunday, major to extreme coastal flooding is expected, with an impactful storm forecast to affect the region on Tuesday and Wednesday.

    The NWS predicts the San Francisco tide gauge could reach 8.4 feet on Tuesday, and 8.6 feet (2.6 meters) on Wednesday, above mean lower low water. Thursday's predicted level is 8.2 feet (2.5 meters). These figures include the forecast tidal conditions, with additional storm-related water potentially worsening the situation. The previous record at San Francisco's Crissy Field gauge was 8.66 feet (2.63 meters), recorded in January 1983, according to the Los Angeles Times.

    In a recent development, the implications extend beyond airport infrastructure. Highway 101, an key access route for SFO passengers, could also experience flooding, potentially making it difficult for travelers and airport employees to reach the terminals. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has urged residents to avoid unnecessary journeys, particularly between Monday afternoon and Wednesday. The city is also suspending parking meter and time-limit enforcement during that period to help residents move their vehicles away from vulnerable areas, according to Deep Arrival.

    The timing could hardly be worse for the airport, with Thanksgiving traditionally generating substantial domestic travel demand across the US. Any flooding affecting SFO's runways, taxiways, or surrounding access roads could complicate an already busy operating environment. However, officials have not confirmed that flight cancellations or runway closures will be necessary, and the airport is continuing its preparations to maintain safe operations.

    OAK nearby is also monitoring the situation, although its infrastructure appears better positioned to withstand the predicted water levels. Deep Arrival reports that the airport has raised its perimeter dike to 13 feet (four meters), reaching 17 feet (five meters) in certain locations, and does not presently expect flooding. Meanwhile, the NWS anticipates drier conditions on Thanksgiving Day itself before another storm system potentially arrives during the following weekend.

    Industry observers note that officials are urging passengers to monitor airline notifications and airport updates. The greatest concern is around late-morning high tides on Tuesday and Wednesday, when storm surge could push water beyond vulnerable seawall sections. Although flooding remains a forecast risk, not a confirmed operational disruption, the combination of high water levels and Thanksgiving passenger volumes presents a serious challenge for the airport and could disrupt travelers.

    #76883. How Much Narrower Economy Seats Get When Airlines Fly 10-Abreast Cabins

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1519 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    How Much Narrower Economy Seats Get When Airlines Fly 10-Abreast Cabins

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The discussion of how narrow economy-class seats are when fitted 10-abreast vs.
    • The A330 (including A330neo) and Boeing 787 airliners are typically nine-abreast aircraft, although some earlier mainline Boeing 787s were configured eight-abreast in economy.
    • According to recent reports, both the Boeing 777 and the Airbus A350 were originally designed for nine-abreast seating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The discussion of how narrow economy-class seats are when fitted 10-abreast vs. nine-abreast is largely restricted to the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350. These two aircraft cabins are sized so that they are variously configured nine-abreast or 10-abreast. The massive A380 was wide enough so that it was only fitted with 10-abreast economy seating. Nine-abreast was unnecessary for the Superjumbo, even for premium-heavy mainline carriers, while regulations preclude any consideration of 11-abreast configuration.

    The A330 (including A330neo) and Boeing 787 airliners are typically nine-abreast aircraft, although some earlier mainline Boeing 787s were configured eight-abreast in economy. Today, Japan Airlines remains the only airline to configure its flagship Dreamliners eight-abreast. The A330 and 787 are not realistically wide enough for a 10-abreast configuration.

    According to recent reports, both the Boeing 777 and the Airbus A350 were originally designed for nine-abreast seating. The Boeing 777 was developed as a luxury long-haul aircraft that would offer relatively generous seat width with a 3-3-3 layout. This made it one of the more comfortable high-capacity widebodies. The original 777s came with an internal cabin width of around 19 feet, 3 inches (5.87 meters). They were all configured nine-abreast.

    Later, Boeing 777-200LRs and -300ERs widened this to 19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters). The A350 followed almost two decades after the 777 originally entered service and followed a similar philosophy. But while it was called the 'Xtra Wide Body' (XWB), Airbus trimmed its width relative to the Triple Seven. Its width was considered spacious enough for a comfortable nine-seat economy configuration.

    According to recent reports, these Airbus A350s were built with an internal cabin width of 18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters). The old-production standard A350s were wider than the early Boeing 777s, but they also came at a later time when pressures for denser seating had increased. All these aircraft were physically and legally capable of fitting ten abreast (3-4-3), but airlines chose not to.

    In a recent development, as a rule of thumb, low-cost airlines concentrate on regional travel with the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 families. Long-haul international routes have been the domain of mainline carriers. Low-cost carriers work in a market segment that pushes for denser seating to reduce the cost per seat. Meanwhile, mainline carriers put more emphasis on premium seating and their premium brands. However, some low-cost carriers have moved into the long-haul leisure route market segment.

    Industry observers note that the two sister low-cost, long-haul, leisure airlines, Air Caraïbes and French Bee, have both purchased fleets of A350s. These are original production A350s, and both use the 3-4-3 (10-abreast) economy seating layout. This allows Frenchbee to achieve the A350-1000's maximum certified seat count of 480 (40 premium and 440 economy). Air Caraïbes also has the same configuration on some of its A350-1000s.

    19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters).

    19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters).

    19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters).

    According to recent reports, not standardized (approx. 18+ inches).

    19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters).

    18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters).

    18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters).

    18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters).

    18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters).

    According to recent reports, the result is rather squishy. The published seat width for these economy seats is around 16 inches (41 cm). For reference, the industry average across the airline industry for economy class seats is 17 to 18 inches (about 43–46 cm). These two low-cost airlines are the only ones to have configured their old production A350s in this way. They can because their marketing is not so much concerned with onboard comfort; it's about getting passengers to far-flung leisure destinations as cheaply as possible. Just endure the flight.

    It has been revealed that historically, airlines configured their Boeing 777-200LRs and 777-300ERs nine-abreast (3-3-3), giving economy class passengers 18–18.5 inches (46–47 cm) in seat width. At the same time, market forces increasingly favored a high-density economy-class cabin. This generation of 777 was around four inches (nine cm) wider than the older aircraft.

    In a recent development, today, most of the world's 777-300ERs have been fitted or retrofitted to seat 10-abreast, cutting the seat width to approximately 17 inches (43 cm). Some carriers have resisted the trend, notably Japan Airlines, ANA, Korean Air, and Singapore Airlines. But most, including premium-branded airlines like Qatar and Emirates, are now 10-abreast.

    In a recent development, but even with the nine-abreast hold-outs, it has sometimes not been for the want of trying. In September 2025, Korea's JoongAng reported, "Korean Air is reconsidering its proposal to change the seating layout in economy class from a “3-3-3” to a tighter “3-4-3” arrangement after a mounting backlash from consumers." Korean Air has not yet published a final seat map or official cabin configuration for its ordered Boeing 777-9 aircraft, but it would be surprising if it retains the nine-abreast configuration.

    At 19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters), the 777-300ER was already wide enough for most mainline carriers to configure economy class 10-abreast. The incoming Boeing 777-9 and 777-8 (777X) come with thinner walls, allowing them to have a cabin width of 19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters). Boeing actively trolls Airbus and its A350, saying on its 777X product page, "Up to 40 cm (16 inches) wider than the A350.".

    In a recent development, the extra width will give the remaining holdout airlines more freedom to opt for the denser layout. ​​​​​In November 2026, Singapore Airlines declared its fresh 777-9 cabin with 17.6 inches (44.7 cm) for economy seats in a 3-4-3 configuration. The 777-9's cabin is wider and longer than the 777-300ER, but this will not necessarily increase the aircraft's density, as the vast majority of 777-300ERs are already 10-abreast. Ironically, the opposite is almost true because other market forces are pushing for more premium seating.

    The Boeing 777-300ER is certified to carry up to 550 passengers in an ultra-high density layout. The 777-9 has more cabin space to fit even more seats, but Boeing is limiting its maximum exit-limit seat count by 75 seats (to 475) or by 110 seats (to 440), depending on the door configuration. Put another way, the 777-9 is envisioned to have more business and premium economy seats, while the already standard 10-abreast economy will benefit from a few more inches of lateral space. The economy class cabin is expected to shrink.

    It has been revealed that as stated, the old production A350s have an internal cabin width of approximately 18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters). Without introducing a new variant or generation, Airbus introduced a new production standard that increases the usable cabin length and thins the aircraft walls. This allows the new-production standard cabin width to be 18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters). The first new-production standard A350s were delivered in 2022.

    For airlines retaining the nine-abreast seating, it allows the typical economy seat width to grow from approximately 18 inches (46 cm) up to 18.7 inches (47.5 cm). That will be welcome to passengers. However, it also made 10-abreast seating more feasible. These new aircraft with 10-abreast seating can accommodate 17-inch (43 cm) seats, bringing it closer to the conventional industry standard for economy seating.

    Sources indicate that to date, Philippine Airlines appears to be the only mainline carrier to opt for 10-abreast economy on new production standard A350s. It is able to offer up to an inch more in seat width than French bee, but also has to trim more than an inch relative to airlines operating the A350 in nine-abreast. With the airline industry being a game measured in a couple of marginal inches and pressure for dense economy seating, it's possible more carriers will follow suit.

    The Boeing 777 was originally designed as a nine-abreast airliner, but it has since grown by eight inches (17 cm) in cabin width over its life. This has allowed it to transition to a 10-abreast airliner without having to sacrifice much of its original spaciousness. The original economy class seats were around 18–18.5 inches (46–47 cm), and the next generation is expected to be around 18 inches (46 cm). This may not be an improvement for economy class passengers, but it is not catastrophic either.

    The A350 echoes the 777's path, while also being much more constrained. The A350 can be and is configured 10-abreast, but this reduces the seat width to 16–17 inches (41-43 cm). But there is also some degree of an apples-to-oranges comparison here. For economy passengers, the 777-9 doesn't normally have the advantage. They will be configured 10-abreast, while the A350 is almost always nine-abreast.

    The new-production-standard nine-abreast A350 has a meaningful advantage of approximately 1.1 inches (2.8 cm), or 6.25% more seat width per economy passenger compared with a 10-abreast 777-9. This A350's nine-abreast vs. the 777X's 10-abreast comparison is important as it's a better representation of the actual industry standard. It's also worth noting that the A350 is more versatile than the 777X in terms of its missions and airlines. Only a relatively limited number of mainline carriers are purchasing the 777X, while a larger range of airlines, including low-cost airlines, are purchasing (often smaller) A350 fleets.

    Breaking: Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
    • Recent findings suggest that A bill introduced by Sen.
    • According to recent reports, the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Recent findings suggest that A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

    According to recent reports, the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

    The new office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

    Britt, R-Ala., said the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

    It has been revealed that “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting upcoming technologies and gaps between sectors,” she stated in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

    The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide said.

    Sources indicate that the office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

    It has been revealed that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

    The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

    Recent findings suggest that the House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

    Industry observers note that senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

    It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

    “If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide mentioned.

    Why Aerolíneas Argentinas Is Basically An Ultra Low Cost Carrier In Disguise

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1493 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This might seem like a rather niche topic to cover in my first week at OMAAT, but after Ben mentioned this story in his intro article, I thought it made sense to follow up fast with an explainer.
    • As a flag carrier of the 3rd most populous nation in South America, I went into my Aerolíneas Argentinas flight with them at the start of the year expecting some pretty standard things: enjoying my SkyTeam benefits, lounge access, and, most importantly of all for someone living out of a suitcase, checked bag allowance.
    • However, I quickly discovered that the airline is basically an ultra-low-cost airline masquerading as a full-service carrier.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This might seem like a rather niche topic to cover in my first week at OMAAT, but after Ben mentioned this story in his intro article, I thought it made sense to follow up fast with an explainer.

    As a flag carrier of the 3rd most populous nation in South America, I went into my Aerolíneas Argentinas flight with them at the start of the year expecting some pretty standard things: enjoying my SkyTeam benefits, lounge access, and, most importantly of all for someone living out of a suitcase, checked bag allowance.

    However, I quickly discovered that the airline is basically an ultra-low-cost airline masquerading as a full-service carrier.

    In a recent development, I needed to get from Buenos Aires to Mendoza for a friend’s 40th birthday celebrations. Options were pretty limited, with nonstop flights available with either JetSmart or, indeed, Aerolíneas Argentinas. I try to avoid low-cost airlines when possible, because, quite simply, I enjoy the flying experience, and low-cost airlines tend to suck every enjoyable element out of it.

    Other pros to booking Aerolíneas Argentinas, personally:.

    After researching my options, I used Flying Blue miles to book two single tickets from Buenos Aires Jorge Newbery Aeroparque Airport (AEP) to Mendoza’s El Plumerillo Airport (MDZ).

    I can’t remember how much the fares were when I was planning the trip, but each one-way flight cost a total of 7,500 miles and less than $10 in taxes and fees.

    Looking now at example fares for January next year, round-trips for Aerolíneas’ lowest and most restrictive fare category (more on that to come) start at around $120.

    It has been revealed that I know it’s not a hard-and-fast rule, but I’ve come to expect that, most of the time, the baggage allowance listed on the booking confirmation is correct. This is often true with redemptions, such as British Airways, which notably offers and acknowledges a 23 kg baggage allowance when redeeming Avios, even for a short-haul flight in economy.

    The confirmation email I received clearly noted 1x checked bag with a 23 kg limit.

    Again, the attached PDF stated that I’d have 1x checked bag included.

    As the Argentinian scamsters would have it, I learned at check-in that the airline has a 15 kg weight limit for checked bags on domestic flights. I tried to plead my case and highlighted the rather unhelpful check-in agent my booking confirmation, but he basically said, “that means nothing.”.

    So they weigh your bag, give you a ticket, and then you have to exit the terminal building and find this little cashier where they collect their scammy little earnings. And what better place to proudly display a “SkyTeam Alliance Member” sign at the very desk where the airline also proudly collects baggage fees from SkyTeam elite status holders, even when traveling on award tickets?

    It has been revealed that once I’d been charged the fee of around $17, I had to join another queue back inside and show them I’d paid for the extra weight before they’d dispatch my bag. You might look at the $32 in fees I paid and think, “What is he complaining about?” But this isn’t about the actual amount of money; it’s the principle.

    Sources indicate that only after the debacle did I learn the extent of Aerolíneas Argentinas’ domestic fare restrictions. Imagine paying $510 (more than four times the cheapest fare) for a “premium economy” ticket and still only getting 15 kg checked baggage allowance, no Fast Pass, no priority boarding (what?), and no lounge access. The latter isn’t such a big deal as Aerolíneas Argentinas doesn’t even have its own lounge at AEP.

    Airline loyalty is really notable to me, and I generally value it more than the ability to redeem miles. Maybe I’ll get into that another day….

    Things got off to a fairly normal start when I saw the Sky Priority check-in kiosks at Aeroparque.

    That feeling of normalcy lasted as long as it took me to get from the sign to the aforementioned conversation about the checked bag situation at the desk. Despite my very best efforts combining my Castilian Spanish and Geordie charm (we’re called Geordies where I’m from in the North East of England), the man at the check-in desk seemed to take real pleasure in explaining that the checked bag rules on my booking confirmation were irrelevant and I’d have to pay the fee.

    For what it’s worth, Sky Priority check-in was also available at Mendoza.

    Being nickel-and-dimed for a checked bag by a flag carrier airline is shameful.

    Recent findings suggest that back at Aeroparque, there was no fast track, and the security line was ridiculously long. That noted, it’s rare in South America to have fast track lanes. For example, no matter whether you’re flying economy or first class (even Air France La Première), everyone waits in the same line to clear pre-departure passport control at São Paulo’s Guarulhos.

    Thanks to my Priority Pass, I did have access to the surprisingly nice AMAE lounge in the national departures part of the airport.

    Even from the outside, my 15-year-old Embraer 190 looked like it had seen better days. The zebra-striped dirt streaks running from each window suggested this place hadn’t been washed or hit the maintenance hangar for a while.

    According to recent reports, inside the Embraer, however, could have been a lot worse. The older seats had thick padding, and despite being a small 2-2-configured cabin, it felt bright and spacious.

    It was the Uber advertising on every single headrest that I found most jarring.

    It has been revealed that the legroom was decent, too. The retro seatback screens, on the other hand, were pretty much redundant.

    In a recent development, it was stepping on board the 16-year-old Boeing 737-700 back to Buenos Aires that Aerolíneas Argentinas’ low-costness was most glaring. Looking at this, I would never guess this plane belonged to a flag carrier. The seats were very uncomfortable, and I think I remember they didn’t recline either.

    As for service, I don’t recall it being particularly good or particularly bad. Forgettable is probably the most accurate word.

    Industry observers note that imagine the likes of Spirit (RIP) or Ryanair calling itself a national flag carrier; that’s basically what Aerolíneas Argentinas is. I’m planning a trip with my dad and brother for February next year that includes Argentina, and I will actively avoid flying Aerolíneas, even if it means forgoing the chance to earn any Flying Blue miles and XPs.

    In a recent development, it’s almost as if the airline has been abandoned. After all, the only real competition is low-cost airlines at LATAM — the full-service carrier which dominates South America. Who knows, maybe things will change come 2028 when it takes delivery of upcoming Airbus A330-900s and Boeing 737 MAXs.

    In a recent development, if I were a power that be at SkyTeam, I’d definitely remove the airline from the alliance. And if I had my way, Aerolíneas Argentinas would be bought by LATAM, and the cherry on top would be LATAM joining SkyTeam. I should probably put a business case together for that….

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) alert after encountering an unresponsive Cessna while climbing out of Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) last week.
    • Although the encounter triggered an automated collision-avoidance warning, the Air Canada aircraft continued its scheduled journey without diverting or returning to the airport.
    • According to AIRLIVE, AC1769 departed Palm Springs International Airport at 12:45 PM local time on November 17.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) alert after encountering an unresponsive Cessna while climbing out of Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) last week. AC1769, bound for Vancouver International Airport (YVR), reportedly received a resolution advisory at approximately 11,400 feet, prompting its pilots to climb to 12,000 feet to avoid the nearby aircraft. The incident occurred shortly after the aircraft departed Palm Springs, with the smaller aircraft reportedly failing to respond.

    Although the encounter triggered an automated collision-avoidance warning, the Air Canada aircraft continued its scheduled journey without diverting or returning to the airport. The 737 MAX 8 subsequently landed safely in Vancouver. While the incident highlights the importance of onboard collision-avoidance technology, several details surrounding the encounter, including the Cessna's identity and the minimum distance between the two aircraft, remain unknown.

    According to AIRLIVE, AC1769 departed Palm Springs International Airport at 12:45 PM local time on November 17. The aircraft, registered C-FSDB, was a 737 MAX 8 operating a scheduled service to Vancouver. It departed from Runway 31R and began its climb towards cruising altitude when its onboard Traffic Collision Avoidance System detected potentially conflicting traffic.

    The reported encounter involved a small Cessna that was not responding as the Canadian aircraft climbed through approximately 11,400 feet. The TCAS resolution advisory instructed the Air Canada pilots to climb to 12,000 feet, representing an additional 600 feet of altitude. This maneuver was intended to establish greater vertical separation between the two aircraft and resolve the potential traffic conflict.

    Importantly, the reported alert was a resolution advisory (RA), not a proximity warning. According to AeroSillage, an RA provides pilots with instructions to modify or maintain their vertical flight path to address a potential collision threat. The available reports do not establish the exact distance between the aircraft when the alert occurred.

    According to recent reports, TCAS is an important layer of aviation safety, particularly when aircraft encounter potentially conflicting traffic in busy airspace. The technology uses information transmitted by nearby aircraft transponders to identify potential collision threats. Depending on the circumstances, the system can problem traffic advisories or resolution advisories, recommending that pilots climb or descend to increase vertical separation.

    It has been revealed that unlike instructions from air traffic controllers, TCAS resolution advisories are generated automatically using onboard surveillance equipment. According to the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Aeronautical Information Manual, pilots are expected to follow an RA promptly unless doing so would jeopardize the aircraft's safety. However, the circumstances surrounding the Cessna's reported lack of response remain unclear. AeroSillage noted that the available reporting does not establish whether the smaller aircraft failed to answer a radio communication or did not comply with an air traffic controller's instruction. Its registration, the nature of the communication attempts, and the minimum separation between the aircraft have not been disclosed.

    Industry observers note that despite the reported encounter, AC1769 continued its journey to Canada without an emergency diversion. AIRLIVE reported that the aircraft landed at Vancouver International Airport at 4:45 PM local time, completing the approximately two-hour-and-40-minute journey. Flight-tracking information independently confirms that this 737 MAX 8 operated the Palm Springs-Vancouver service and reached its destination. No other details or further emergency involving the aircraft were reported. Nevertheless, the incident illustrates how unexpected traffic conflicts can require immediate action even during otherwise routine departures.

    In a recent development, based on available reporting, no specific findings from the US or Canadian authorities have established the circumstances of the encounter. Without an official reconstruction, it remains impossible to determine whether the Cessna experienced a communication problem, whether an instruction was missed, or how close the aircraft actually came.

    End Of An Era: American Retires Boeing 777 Flagship First Class

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American Airlines has just officially “retired” its Flagship First product on the Boeing 777-300ER, meaning that no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore.
    • As I’ve covered in the past, American is in the process of eliminating its “premium” first class product, and that change was just implemented for flights as of this week on the carrier’s biggest planes.
    • Specifically, the Boeing 777-300ER is American’s “flagship” aircraft, with 20 of the planes in the fleet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines has just officially “retired” its Flagship First product on the Boeing 777-300ER, meaning that no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore. The good news is that an updated business class product is in the process of being rolled out, and that’s something that should benefit a lot of travelers.

    As I’ve covered in the past, American is in the process of eliminating its “premium” first class product, and that change was just implemented for flights as of this week on the carrier’s biggest planes.

    Specifically, the Boeing 777-300ER is American’s “flagship” aircraft, with 20 of the planes in the fleet. As of this week, the airline is no longer selling first class on these planes. Now, plenty of 777-300ERs with these cabins are still flying around, as American has just started reconfiguring its 777-300ERs with new cabins, including the new business class.

    According to recent reports, still, for flights effective immediately, first class seats are just being sold as standard business class seats, and any business class passenger can select seats in the first two rows (you’d think they’d try to charge extra or at least reserve them for select elite members, but nope). So there will no longer be a differentiated soft product… not that there was much of a difference as of late anyway!

    With this change, no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore either, so it very much is the end of an era. American’s 777 first class seats were controversial — on the one hand, I kind of love how they swivel, though on the other hand, they really lack privacy, and the soft product left a lot to be desired.

    Sources indicate that I expect we’ll continue to see these planes flying around well into late 2027, or possibly even into 2028, depending on how fast the retrofit project happens. American’s dedicated first class ground product has also largely been discontinued, as Flagship First Dining has turned into Flagship Dining, so a la carte lounge dining is now available to eligible business class passengers as well.

    It’s great that these planes will be getting new business class suites, as they’ll also be the aircraft belonging to a US carrier with the most business class seats, as they’ll have 70 of them… that’s lot!

    While American has now eliminated its international first class product, it’s worth emphasizing that the airline still technically has a “premium” first class, in the sense of a cabin above business class.

    It has been revealed that specifically, American still has its specially configured Airbus A321T aircraft, which are used primarily for flights between Upcoming York (JFK) and Los Angeles (LAX) and San Francisco (SFO). The planes have 10 reverse herringbone seats spread across five rows, in a 1-1 configuration.

    American also intends to eliminate this product, as the A321Ts will be reconfigured into standard A321 domestic configuration aircraft, and A321XLRs will be taking over the transcon routes.

    American has stopped selling first class on these planes for flights as of March 28, 2027. After that date we’ll still see some of the planes flying with the cabins, but the first class seats will simply be sold as business class.

These planes are being retrofitted, as first class seats are being eliminated, and latest business class suites are being introduced. However, the planes will keep flying around with the current cabins for quite some time, and business class passengers can freely assign the first class seats.

    In the spring, we’ll see American eliminate its last “premium” first class product, which is the A321T first class cabin, as those planes are replaced by A321XLRs.

    We’ve just seen American formally retire its Boeing 777 first class, and with that, no airline in the United States has a “true” international first class anymore. It’s the end of an era, because going back many decades, premium products were largely pioneered by US carriers. So I think this raises the question — why can US carriers not make first class work in a way that’s economically viable, especially as they keep talking about how premium they are?

    Before we get into this, let me make sure we’re all on the same page when it comes to terms. This post isn’t about the premium cabin on domestic flights, which is often referred to as first class. Instead, it’s about international flights that have a cabin above business class, when it’s marketed as first class. So this would include airlines on my list of the world’s best first class products.

    Sources indicate that airline executives are divided on the merits of having an international first class cabin. Some insist that there’s no need for such a cabin, as business class has improved so much. Meanwhile others absolutely see merit to such a product.

    What’s interesting is that for the airlines that succeed with first class, the single biggest market — and single biggest point of sale — is the United States. So how is it that carriers like Air France, Lufthansa, SWISS, etc., can make money offering first class to the United States (primarily targeting Americans), but US airlines seemingly can’t?

    The US has way too many people with tens or hundreds of millions of dollars, or even billions of dollars. There are plenty of people who would pay to fly private, and would pay for Air France La Premiere first class, but would never consider paying the high price for first class on a US carrier, because it’s just not worth it.

    When they fly first class, they want this….

    It has been revealed that it’s no surprise that first class at US carriers has historically failed. In many ways, it reflects the failures of the industry from decades past. In other words, first class has long been thought of as “upgrade class,” rather than something actually worth paying for. US carriers have managed to change that narrative on domestic flights, but not so much on international flights.

    In terms of economics, let me also point out that the opportunity cost of a first class cabin isn’t actually that high. “Premium” is all the rage, so what you do here is eliminate some economy seats:.

    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
    • According to recent reports, jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no declared opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    According to recent reports, jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no declared opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries mentioned at a press conference following the election.

    It has been revealed that while Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get big things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    Sources indicate that “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    In a recent development, “This is the beginning of a upcoming bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., said at the press conference.

    Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the newly introduced majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    Industry observers note that at his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    Sources indicate that “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had said they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    Pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    It has been revealed that the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries remarked Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he stated at his news conference.

    • Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S.

    According to recent reports, the British first edition of The Managerial Revolution that I picked up in a Charing Cross Road shop a quarter century ago tells us much about the work itself. I’ve read it four times, conscripted it as an airplane companion, and brought it to the beach. Yet its binding remains strong, its cover quite flexible, and its pages yellowing but intact. We no longer much refer to let alone read such 1941 bestsellers as Clifton Fadiman’s Reading I’ve Liked or Margaret Leech’s Reveille in Washington. But James Burnham, much like my strong and solid copy of his most famous book, endures.

    Burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation. The Managerial Revolution, anticipating as it did the ascension of technocrats, specialists, and the bureaucratic elite as a sort of ruling class, surely helped in that regard. Burnham remains read, despite no Burnhamite clique in academia or organized faction among movement conservatives dedicated to advancing his ideas. Kirkians, Straussians, and Randians exist. Why no James Burnham Preservation Society with an accompanying secret handshake?

    It has been revealed that daniel J. Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S. Meyer, is an American Spectator senior editor, visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution, and YouTuber @RightWingWilderness.

    On “The Complex Reputation of James Burnham”.
